data.text: You are a word master! Should we review the rules once more, or continue our journey to the village?

data.speaker: polly
data.text: Look at the bus! I am thinking of traveling, but Manya is planning. He is using the GOING TO structure to show his intent!

rules.title: The SVA Rule
rules.formula: Subject + Correct Helping Verb + GOING TO
rules.exampleB: Polly and Manya are going to cook.
rules.teacherNote: Always check if the subject is singular or plural before picking the helping verb.

rules.title: Intention vs. Will
rules.exampleA: I am going to visit the rural area.
rules.explainA: This means I have already packed my bags.
rules.explainB: This is just a general statement.
rules.teacherNote: In PLE, 'going to' is often used to show a planned vacation.

data.speaker: kiki
data.text: While we ride, let's play Question Tags. If the statement is positive, the tag is negative. It’s like a mirror, isn't it?

rules.title: The 'I AM' Trap
rules.explainB: In a negative tag, it stays 'am I'.
rules.teacherNote: UNEB loves this! NEVER write 'amn't I?'. It is always 'aren't I?'

rules.title: The 'Let's' Trap
rules.exampleB: Let us go to the pond, shall we?
rules.explainB: It doesn't matter if it's 'Let us' or 'Let's'.
rules.teacherNote: This is a fixed rule. Even if the statement is positive, the tag is 'shall we?'

rules.title: Hidden Negatives
rules.explainA: Words like 'hardly', 'seldom', and 'rarely' make the sentence negative.
rules.explainB: Since the sentence is negative, the tag MUST be positive.
rules.teacherNote: If you see 'hardly', do not use a 'not' in the tag!

data.speaker: manya
data.text: Wait! Polly is telling everyone what the teacher said. She is using Reported Speech! You must shift the tense back in time.

rules.title: Rule 1: The Tense Shift
rules.exampleB: Polly said that she <u>was</u> ready to board.
rules.explainA: The verb 'am' is in the present.
rules.explainB: When reporting, 'am' shifts back to the past: 'was'.
rules.teacherNote: PLE TRAP: If the speaker is a girl (Polly), 'I' must change to 'she'!

rules.title: Rule 2: Future & Modals
rules.formula: will → would | can → could | must → had to
rules.exampleB: Kiki said that she <u>would</u> help with chores.
rules.explainA: The helping verb 'will' shows the future.
rules.explainB: 'Will' always changes to 'would' in reported speech.
rules.teacherNote: Other changes: 'Can' becomes 'Could' and 'Must' becomes 'Had to'.

rules.title: Rule 3: Time & Place Shifts
rules.formula: now → then | today → that day | tomorrow → the next day
rules.exampleB: Manya said that he was traveling <u>that day</u>.
rules.explainA: Words like 'today' or 'now' are specific to the moment.
rules.explainB: In reports, we change them to show the time has passed.
rules.teacherNote: This is a major PLE target! Students often forget to change 'today' to 'that day'.

rules.title: Rule 4: The 'That' Connector
rules.explainA: Direct speech uses a comma and quotation marks.
rules.explainB: Reported speech removes the marks and uses 'that' as a bridge.
rules.teacherNote: Always remove the exclamation marks or question marks when reporting a statement!

data.speaker: kiki
data.text: We are here! The village is so BEAUTIFUL. 'Beautiful' is an ADJECTIVE. I can make more adjectives by adding suffixes like -ful or -ing!

rules.title: Suffix -ful (Full of)
rules.teacherNote: PLE TRAP: Never write 'beautifull'. The adjective suffix -ful has only one 'L'!

rules.title: Suffix -ing (Describing)
rules.teacherNote: Remember: We use -ing for the THING and -ed for the FEELING. (The trip is exciting; Manya is excited).
